zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كانَ يَظُنُّ أنْ لَنْ يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾ — this hāʾ (the pronoun "him") refers to Muhammad ﷺ, i.e. "Whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muhammad ﷺ until He makes it prevail over all religion, let him die of rage." That is the explanation of His saying: ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إلى السَّماءِ﴾. "السبب" is the rope, and "السماء" is the ceiling, i.e. let him tie a rope fast to his ceiling, then cut — that is, let him stretch the rope until it is cut off, so that he dies strangled. ﴿هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ ما يَغِيظُ﴾, i.e. will his scheme remove his rage? It has been read "ثُمَّ لِيَقْطَعْ" and "ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ", with kasra on the lām and with it vowelless (sukūn).

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا والَّذِينَ هادُوا والصّابِئِينَ والنَّصارى والمَجُوسَ والَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾: Allah will judge between these five sects and the believers.
﴿فالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهم ثِيابٌ مِن نارٍ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 19], while the believers enter Paradise, and that is His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 23]. The khabar (predicate) of the first "إنَّ" is the whole clause together with the second "إنَّ". Some people have claimed that your saying "إنَّ زَيْدًا إنَّهُ قائِمٌ" is poor usage, and that this verse is only acceptable because of "الَّذِي" (the relative noun). But there is no difference between "الذي" and anything else in the chapter of "إنَّ": if you say "إنَّ زَيْدًا إنَّهُ قائِمٌ", it is good. Like it is the poet's saying:
؎إنَّ الخَلِيفَةَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَرْبَلَهُ
(Indeed the caliph — indeed Allah has clothed him…)
There is no disagreement among the Basrans that "إنَّ" may enter upon every mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar: you say "إنَّ زَيْدًا هو قائِمٌ" and "إنَّ زَيْدًا إنَّهُ قائِمٌ".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ والنُّجُومُ والجِبالُ والشَّجَرُ والدَّوابُّ وكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النّاسِ وكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العَذابُ﴾: prostration here is submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and it is obedience from those whom Allah has created, both living creatures and inanimate things.
The proof that it is a prostration of obedience is His saying: ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النّاسِ وكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العَذابُ﴾. This is the best of the interpretations: that it prostrates in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَقالَ لَها ولِلأرْضِ ائْتِيا طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا قالَتا أتَيْنا طائِعِينَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 11], and as He said: "وَإنَّ مِنها — meaning the stones — لَما يَهْبِطُ مِن خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ". Fear can only exist through what Allah has given it, by which He tests its fear.
Some people said: the prostration of these things which are inanimate, and of the animals that have no reason, is only the trace of the craftsmanship in them, and the submissiveness which shows that they are created. They cited as proof for this the poet's saying:
؎بِجَيْشٍ يَضِلُّ البُلْقُ في حَجَراتِهِ تُرى الأُكْمُ فِيها سُجَّدًا لِلْحَوافِرِ
(With an army in whose flanks the piebald horses are lost, in which the hillocks are seen prostrate before the hooves.)
That is, they have become humbled by the treading of the hooves upon them. They said this because, in their view, prostration that is obedience can only come from one who has reason. What breaks this is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, described: that among the stones there are some that fall down out of fear of Allah; and fear and dread we have only understood of human beings, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed us that among the stones there are some that fear Him. And He informed us that He subjected the mountains and the birds together with Dāwūd, glorifying with him. If the glorification of the mountains and birds were the trace of craftsmanship, it would not have been said "سَخَّرْنا" (We subjected), nor "مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ" (with Dāwūd the mountains), because the trace of craftsmanship is evident with Dāwūd and others alike. So it is without doubt a prostration of obedience, and likewise the glorification in the mountains and birds; but we do not know their glorification unless it comes to us in a hadith how that glorification is. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44].

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَذانِ خَصْمانِ اخْتَصَمُوا في رَبِّهِمْ﴾: the two disputing parties are the believers and the unbelievers. It came in the exegesis that the Jews said to the Muslims: "Our religion is older than your religion, and our Book is older than your Book." The Muslims answered them with: "We believe in what was sent down to us and what was sent down to you, and we believe in Allah, His angels, His Books and His messengers, making no distinction between any of His messengers, while you have disbelieved in some of the messengers." So the argument of the Muslims prevailed over the unbelievers. It says "اخْتَصَمُوا" (plural), though it said "خَصْمانِ" (dual), because they are two groups. ﴿فالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهم ثِيابٌ مِن نارٍ﴾: it came in the exegesis that the garments of fire are copper that has been melted. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ الحَمِيمُ﴾ ﴿يُصْهَرُ بِهِ ما في بُطُونِهِمْ والجُلُودُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 20]: what is in their bellies boils from it until it comes out of their rear ends. This is for one of the two disputing parties.

zajjaj:23-23.t: And He said concerning the disputing party who are believers: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ ولُؤْلُؤًا﴾ — and "لُؤْلُؤٍ": both are read. Whoever reads "وَلُؤْلُؤًا" takes it in the sense of "they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and they will be adorned with pearls"; and whoever reads "وَلُؤْلُؤٍ" means "and of pearls". It is also possible that it is "bracelets of gold and pearl", so that there is in them a mixture of the two kinds. It is also read "يَحْلَوْنَ فِيها", in the sense of your saying "حَلِيَ، يَحْلى" when one comes to have jewellery.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ويَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ والمَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنّاسِ سَواءً العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ ومَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾: the form "يَصُدُّونَ" is an imperfect (future) form conjoined to a past form, because the meaning of "الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" is "those who are unbelievers"; so it is as though He said: "Indeed the unbelievers and those who bar…". Concerning the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" there are two views. One is that it is omitted, so that the meaning is: "Indeed those of this description have perished."
It is also possible — and this is the preferred view — that the khabar is "نُذِقْهُ مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ", so the meaning is: "Indeed the unbelievers and those who deviate in the Sacred Mosque, We shall make them taste a painful punishment." As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سَواءً العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ﴾, the reading is the nominative (rafʿ) in "سَواءٌ", and its nominative is from two angles. One is that the complete stop is at ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنّاسِ﴾, as He said: ﴿إنَّ أوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنّاسِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 96],
and then ﴿سَواءً العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. It may also be on the pattern of "جَعَلْناهُ سَواءٌ العاكِفُ فِيهِ", so that "سَواءٌ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar here is "العاكِفُ فِيهِ" — I mean the khabar of "سَواءٌ" is "العاكِفُ" — and the clause is the khabar (second object) of "جَعَلْناهُ". [Translator's note: the source says "the reading is the nominative in سَواءٌ" while the verse is quoted with the accusative سَواءً; it is translated as written.]
The explanation of His saying ﴿سَواءً العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ﴾ is that the one residing in Mecca and the one who travels to it from whatever land are equal in dwelling there. It has also been said: "Equal in its merit and in performing the rites are the one devoted to it, residing in the Sanctuary, and the one who travels to it."
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾: it has been said that "deviation (الإلحاد) in it" is associating partners with Allah; and it has been said that every wrongdoer in it is a deviator (مُلْحِد). It has come from ʿUmar that hoarding food in Mecca is ilḥād. The lexicographers said that the meaning of the bāʾ is that it is to be dropped (redundant), the meaning being: "and whoever intends in it deviation through wrongdoing (إلْحادًا بِظُلْمٍ)", and they recited the poet's saying:
؎هُنَّ الحَرائِرُ لا رَبّاتُ أحْمِرَةٍ سُودُ المَحاجِرِ لا يَقْرَأْنَ بِالسُّوَرِ
(They are free-born women, not owners of donkeys, black around the eyes, who do not recite the suras.)
The meaning according to them is "they do not recite the suras (لا يَقْرَأْنَ السُّوَرَ)". And they recited:
؎بِوادٍ يَمانٍ يُنْبِتُ البَثَّ فَرْعُهُ ∗∗∗ وأسْفَلُهُ بِالمَرْخِ والشَّبَهانِ
(In a Yemeni valley whose upper part grows al-baththa, and its lower part markh and shabahān.)
That is: "and its lower part grows markh and shabahān". What our colleagues (the Basrans) hold is that the bāʾ is not redundant; the meaning according to them is: "and whoever's intention in it is that he deviate through wrongdoing (بِأنْ يُلْحِدَ بِظُلْمٍ)". It is like his saying:
؎أُرِيدُ لِأنْسى ذِكْرَها فَكَأنَّما ∗∗∗ تَمَثَّلُ لِي لَيْلى بِكُلِّ سَبِيلِ
(I want to forget her memory, yet it is as though Laylā takes form before me on every path.)
The meaning is: "I want, and my wanting is for this." And the meaning of "الإلحاد" in the language is turning away from the right course.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذْ بَوَّأْنا لإبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ البَيْتِ﴾: We made the place of the House an abode (مُبَوَّأ) for Ibrāhīm; "المُبَوَّأ" is the dwelling place. The meaning is that Allah made known to Ibrāhīm the place of the House, so he built the House upon its ancient foundation. In the days of the Flood the House had been raised up to heaven, when Allah drowned the earth and what was on it; so He honoured His House by removing it from the totality of what was drowned. It is narrated that the House was of a red ruby.
His saying: ﴿وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطّائِفِينَ والقائِمِينَ﴾: it has been said that the meaning is "purify it of polytheism"; and "القائمون" here are those who pray.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأذِّنْ في النّاسِ بِالحَجِّ﴾: it is narrated that Ibrāhīm's proclamation of the pilgrimage was that he stood at the Station (al-Maqām) and said: "O people, respond, O servants of Allah! Obey Allah, O servants of Allah! Fear Allah!" It settled in the heart of every believing man and woman, and it made all between heaven and earth hear it, and those in the loins (of their fathers) for whom pilgrimage was written answered him; so everyone who performs the pilgrimage is among those who answered Ibrāhīm. It is also narrated that his proclamation of the pilgrimage was: "O people, the pilgrimage has been prescribed for you." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ رِجالا وعَلى كُلِّ ضامِرٍ﴾: "رِجالًا" is the plural of "راجِل" (one on foot), like "صاحِب" and "صِحاب", and "قائِم" and "قِيام". ﴿وَعَلى كُلِّ ضامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ﴾, i.e. they will come to you on foot and riding. He said "يَأْتِينَ" (feminine plural) according to the sense of camels; the meaning is: "and on every lean camel (بَعِير ضامِر) coming from every deep (عَمِيق) mountain pass". "عَمِيق" means far. Ruʾba said:
؎وَقاتِمِ الأعْماقِ خاوِي المُخْتَرَقْ
(And many a dusky-depthed [desert], empty where one cuts across it.)
"الأعْماق" are the far bottoms; and from this it is said: "this is a deep (عَمِيقَة) well", i.e. far in its bottom. [Translator's note: the source text has «بَعِيد ضامِر» in the paraphrase, which is apparently a copying error for «بَعِير ضامِر» (a lean camel); translated according to the context.]

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنافِعَ لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. that they may witness what Allah has urged them towards, wherein is benefit for them in their Hereafter. ﴿وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ في أيّامٍ مَعْلُوماتٍ عَلى ما رَزَقَهم مِن بَهِيمَةِ الأنْعامِ﴾: by this is meant the Day of Sacrifice and the days after it on which sacrifice is made, because the mention (of Allah's name) here indicates the naming (of Allah) over what is slaughtered, on account of His saying: ﴿عَلى ما رَزَقَهم مِن بَهِيمَةِ الأنْعامِ﴾. And His saying: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنها وأطْعِمُوا البائِسَ الفَقِيرَ﴾: "البائِس" is one who has been afflicted by hardship (بُؤْس), and "البُؤْس" is severe poverty. One says "قَدْ بَؤُسَ، وبَأْسَ" when one comes into hardship.
His saying ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنها﴾ is not a binding command: whoever wishes may eat from his sacrifice and whoever wishes may not eat; it is only a permission, as He said: ﴿وَإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 2]. He only said "فاصْطادُوا" (then hunt) because He had prohibited hunting to them while they were in iḥrām, and then He permitted them hunting. Likewise this command here is a permission after they had forbidden themselves to eat the sacrificial animals, because the people of the Jāhiliyya, when they made a sacrifice, did not consider it lawful to eat anything of their sacrifices; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this is permissible.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهم ولْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ﴾: it has been read "ثُمَّ لِيَقْضُوا" with kasra on the lām, and that is how Abū ʿAmr read it; the reading with sukūn after "ثُمَّ" is common. "التَّفَث" came in the exegesis, and the lexicographers know it only from the exegesis. They said: "التفث" is trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair and cutting the hair — as though it were the passage out of iḥrām into the state of release. His saying: ﴿وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا بِالبَيْتِ العَتِيقِ﴾:
several views have been stated about "العَتِيق". Al-Ḥasan said: it is the ancient House, and al-Ḥasan's proof for this is His saying: ﴿إنَّ أوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبارَكًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 96]. It has also been said that "the ʿatīq House" is the one that was freed (عُتِقَ) from drowning in the days of the Flood, and the proof of this view is: ﴿وَإذْ بَوَّأْنا لإبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ البَيْتِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 26], which is proof that the House was raised and its place remained.
Most of what came in the exegesis is that it was freed from the tyrants, so no tyrant ever gained mastery over it. It has been said that it was called "العَتِيق" because no one among people ever owned it. And it has been said it was only called "العَتِيق" because no tyrant ever aimed at it but that Allah destroyed him. One says: "أعْتَقْتُ المَمْلُوكَ، فَهو مُعْتَقٌ، وعَتِيقٌ" (I freed the slave, so he is freed, ʿatīq). Everything that has passed in the explanation of "العتيق" is permissible and good — and Allah knows best the reality of that. This verse indicates that the circumambulation on the Day of Sacrifice is obligatory. [Translator's note: the source has «لَمْ يَدَعْهُ أحَدٌ» ("no one claimed it"), apparently for «لم يملكه أحد» or «لم يَدَّعِه»; rendered as "owned"/claimed according to the sense.]

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ ومَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُماتِ اللَّهِ﴾: the sacred ordinances (حُرُمات) of Allah are the pilgrimage, the ʿumra and the rest of the rites; everything Allah has made obligatory is among the ḥurumāt of Allah. "الحُرْمَة" is what one is obliged to carry out and whose neglect and abandonment are forbidden. The position of "ذَلِكَ" is nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is: "the matter is that".
His saying: ﴿وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ الأنْعامُ إلا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: "ما" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. "except what is recited to you": carrion, blood, the strangled, the beaten to death, and the rest of what has been recited as forbidden.
His saying: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾: "مِن" here is for singling out one genus from among genera; the meaning is: "so avoid the filth that is idols".
His saying: ﴿واجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ﴾: "الزُّور" is lying; and it has been said that here it is associating partners with Allah.
It has also been said: false testimony. All of this is permissible. The verse indicates — and Allah knows best — that they were forbidden to declare unlawful what the idolaters declared unlawful, such as their saying: ﴿ما في بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا ومُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أزْواجِنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 139], and such as their sacrificing the baḥīra and the sāʾiba. So Allah made known to them that cattle are lawful except what Allah has forbidden of them, and Allah forbade them false speech: that they should say "This is lawful and this is forbidden", so as to fabricate lies against Allah.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿حُنَفاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its interpretation is: "being Muslims, not inclining to any religion other than Islam".
His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِ ومَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَكَأنَّما خَرَّ مِنَ السَّماءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ﴾: it is read "فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ" and "فَتَخَطِّفُهُ", and al-Ḥasan read "فَتِخِطِّفُهُ" with kasra on the tāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ. Whoever reads "فَتَخْطَفُهُ" without doubling takes it from "خَطِفَ يَخْطَفُ", and "الخَطْف" is seizing quickly. Whoever reads "فَتَخَطِّفُهُ" with kasra on the ṭāʾ and doubling, the base form is "فَتَخْتَطِفُهُ": he assimilated the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ and cast the vowel of the tāʾ onto the khāʾ, giving it a fatḥa. Whoever says it with kasra on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ gave the khāʾ kasra because it was vowelless and the (first) ṭāʾ was vowelless. And whoever gives kasra to the tāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ — and that is the reading of al-Ḥasan — does so on the basis that the base form is "تَخْتَطِفُهُ". This is a parable Allah has struck for the unbeliever in his remoteness from the truth: Allah made known that the remoteness from the truth of one who associates partners with Him is like the remoteness of one who falls from the sky and the birds carry him off, or the wind sweeps him down into a far-off (سَحِيق) place, i.e. a distant one.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ ومَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإنَّها مِن تَقْوى القُلُوبِ﴾: "the شَعائِر of Allah" are the waymarks (of religion) which He urged and commanded to be upheld; their singular is "شَعِيرَة". So al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the shaʿāʾir of Allah, and what is meant here is the sacrificial camels (البُدْن).

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿لَكم فِيها مَنافِعُ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّها إلى البَيْتِ العَتِيقِ﴾ means that you have benefits in the sacrificial camels before you mark them and name them as an offering (هَدْي) to My House; then when you have marked them (أشْعَرْتُمُوها) — and the ishʿār is that one slits the hump until it bleeds and hangs a sandal on it, so that it is known to be a sacrificial camel (بَدَنَة) —
most people do not hold it permissible to benefit from it once it has been made a badana: neither from its milk, nor its hair, nor riding its back. One says: "He is not to give its milk, its hair or its back to anyone", because it is a badana, so none but the people of Allah may benefit from it, except in a necessity in which death is feared. Some of them say that he may benefit from it: one who is exhausted may ride it, and he may make use of its benefits until the time of its lawful destination (مَحِلّ) — the place of its sacrifice.
The proof for this is «that the Prophet ﷺ passed by a man driving a badana and ordered him ﷺ to ride it; he said: "It is a badana." He ordered him a second time and ordered him a third time, and said to him the third time: "Ride it, woe to you!"».
It is possible that the Prophet ﷺ saw him compelled to ride it because of severe exhaustion, and it is possible, on the outward sense of the hadith, that riding it is permissible. Whoever permits riding it and benefiting from it says: he may not make it lean or wear it out, because it is a badana.

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنا مَنسَكًا﴾ — it is also read "مَنسِكًا". "المَنسَك" in this place indicates the meaning of sacrificing, so it is as though He said: We appointed for every community that it draw near (to Allah) by slaughtering sacrificial animals for Allah. This is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لِيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلى ما رَزَقَهم مِن بَهِيمَةِ الأنْعامِ﴾, the meaning being: "that they may mention the name of Allah over the sacrifice of the cattle He has provided them". Some of them said: "المَنسَك" is the place which one is obliged to frequent; and that is permissible.
Whoever says "مَنسِك" means by it the place of rites (نُسُك), like "مَجْلِس", the place of sitting; and whoever says "مَنسَك" takes it in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), like "النُّسُك" and "النُّسُوك".
His saying: ﴿فَإلَهُكم إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾, i.e. you must not mention over your sacrifices anyone but Allah alone.
His saying: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ المُخْبِتِينَ﴾: it has been said that "المُخْبِتُون" are the humble; it has been said "المخبتون" are those who are at peace in faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; and it has been said "المخبتون" are those who do not wrong others and, when they are wronged, do not seek revenge. All of that is permissible. Its derivation is from "الخَبْت of the land", which is the low-lying place of it; so every mukhbit is humble.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ﴾: the reading is with the genitive (khafḍ) and dropping the nūn (of the plural) — the genitive being by annexation (iḍāfa). "والمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ" is grammatically possible, except that it is contrary to the codex (muṣḥaf). Also possible — though far-fetched — is "والمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةَ", dropping the nūn and making "الصَّلاةَ" accusative, because of the length of the noun. Sībawayh recited:
؎اَلْحافِظُو عَوْرَةَ العَشِيرَةِ لا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِن ورائِهِمْ نُطَفُ
(Those who guard the exposed flank of the clan — no disgrace comes upon them from behind.)
and he claimed that it is anomalous (shādhdh).

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿والبُدْنَ جَعَلْناها لَكم مِن شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾: the accusative is better, because there is a verb before it. The meaning is: "And We made the sacrificial camels…", so it is made accusative by an implied verb which the overt one explains. If you wish, you may make it nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf). "البُدْن", with sukūn and with ḍamma on the dāl: "بَدَنَة", "بُدْن" and "بُدُن", like his saying "ثَمَرَة", "ثُمْر" and "ثُمُر". It was called "بَدَنَة" only because it grows stout (تَبْدُنُ), i.e. it grows fat.
His saying: ﴿فاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها صَوافَّ﴾: "صَوافَّ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), but it does not take tanwīn because it is a diptote — i.e. its legs having been lined up. That is: mention the name of Allah over them in the state of their sacrifice. The camel is sacrificed standing, and this verse indicates that. It is also read "صَوافِنَ": "الصّافِن" is one that stands on three legs; when they want to sacrifice a camel, one of its forelegs is hobbled, so it is ṣāfin, and the plural is "صَوافِنُ", O you. It has also been read "صَوافِيَ", with yāʾ, with fatḥa, without tanwīn, and its explanation is "خَوالِص", i.e. purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He — do not associate anyone in the naming (of Allah) over their sacrifice.
His saying: ﴿فَإذا وجَبَتْ جُنُوبُها﴾, i.e. when they fall to the ground, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنها وأطْعِمُوا القانِعَ والمُعْتَرَّ﴾, with doubled rāʾ; "والمُعْتَرِي", with yāʾ, is also possible. One says "وَجَبَ الحائِطُ، يَجِبُ، وجْبَةً" when the wall falls; "وَجَبَ القَلْبُ، يَجِبُ، وجْبًا، ووَجِيبًا" when the heart throbs from fright; and "وَجَبَ البَيْعُ، يَجِبُ، وُجُوبًا، وجِبَةً" (the sale became binding). The imperfect in all of this is "يَجِبُ". Concerning "القانِع" it has been said: the one who is content with what you give him; it has been said: the one who is content with little; and it has been said — and this is the view of the lexicographers — the beggar. One says "قَنِعَ الرَّجُلُ، قُنُوعًا" when he begs, so he is qāniʿ; and they recited, by al-Shammākh:
؎لَمالُ المَرْءِ يُصْلِحُهُ فَيُغْنِي مَفاقِرَهُ أعَفُّ مِنَ القُنُوعِ
(A man's wealth, which he manages well so that it relieves his needs, is more honourable than begging.)
i.e. more honourable than asking. And "قَنِعَ، قَناعَةً" when he is satisfied, so he is "قَنِع". "المُعْتَرّ" is the one who comes to you (يَعْتَرِيكَ) and seeks what you have; he asks you when you are asked about asking. Likewise "المُعْتَرِي". [Translator's note: the source vocalises the verb of begging as «قَنِعَ», the same as the verb of contentment; the lexicographers distinguish قَنَعَ قُنُوعًا (to beg) from قَنِعَ قَناعَةً (to be content). The phrase «سَألَكَ إذْ سُئِلْتَ عَنِ السُّؤالِ» appears corrupt in the source and is rendered literally.]

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنْ يَنالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُها ولا دِماؤُها﴾ — it has also been read "لَنْ تَنالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُها" with tāʾ. Whoever reads with yāʾ does so for the plurality of the meat portions, and whoever reads with tāʾ does so for the group of the meat portions. When they slaughtered, they used to smear the House with blood, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that what reaches Him is fear of Him and obedience to Him in what He commands. ﴿وَلَكِنْ يَنالُهُ التَّقْوى مِنكُمْ﴾ and "تَنالُهُ التَّقْوى مِنكُمْ", with yāʾ and tāʾ: whoever makes it feminine does so for the form of "التقوى", and whoever makes it masculine does so because the meaning of "التَّقْوى" and "التُّقى" is one.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدافِعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, also "يَدْفَعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا": this indicates help from Him, i.e. when you repel — that is, when you do this and oppose the people of the Jāhiliyya in what you do regarding their way of sacrificing and their associating partners with Allah — then Allah defends His party.
His saying: ﴿كُلَّ خَوّانٍ كَفُورٍ﴾: "خَوّان" is on the pattern "فَعّال", from "الخِيانَة" (treachery); i.e. whoever mentions the name of other than Allah and draws near to the idols with his sacrifice is a treacherous ingrate. As for "البُدْن", it has been said that they are camels specifically, and it has been said that they are camels and cattle. I know of no one who said that sheep and goats are included in them. As for those who said they are camels and cattle, they are the greatest jurists of the cities; but the usage in driving (offerings) to the House is camels, and that is why those who said they are camels said so.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ﴾ — it is also read "أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ", and it is read "أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ ويُقاتَلُونَ". The meaning is: "Permission has been given to those who fight that they may fight." It is narrated that it was the first verse revealed about fighting. "بِأنَّهم ظُلِمُوا", i.e. they have been permitted to fight because of the wrong done to them.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ﴾: Allah promised them help. It is not permissible to read "وأنَّ اللَّهَ" with fatḥa on "أنَّ", and there is no disagreement among the lexicographers that this is not permissible, because "أنَّ", when the lām accompanies it, is never given fatḥa.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إلا أنْ يَقُولُوا﴾: "الَّذِينَ" is in the position of the genitive (jarr); the meaning is: "Permission has been given to those who were expelled from their homes without right, except that they said 'Our Lord is Allah'". "أنْ" is in the position of the genitive; the meaning is: "they were expelled without right, except for their saying 'Our Lord is Allah'", i.e. they were expelled for nothing but that they affirmed the oneness of Allah; so the idol-worshippers expelled them for their monotheism.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النّاسَ بَعْضَهم بِبَعْضٍ لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوامِعُ﴾: the meaning is: "Were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, monasteries would have been demolished." It is also read "لَهُدِمَتْ". These are the monasteries (صَوامِع) of the monks. ﴿وَبِيَعٌ وصَلَواتٌ ومَساجِدُ﴾: "البِيَع" are the churches of the Christians, and "الصَّلَوات" are the synagogues of the Jews — in Hebrew "صَلُوتا". It has also been read "صَلاةٌ ومَساجِدُ". It has been said that they are the places of prayer of the Sabians. The interpretation of this is: "Were it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, repels some people by others, there would have been demolished, in the law of every prophet, the place in which he prayed." So, were it not for the repelling, there would have been demolished in the time of Mūsā, peace be upon him, the synagogues in which he prayed under his law; in the time of ʿĪsā the monasteries and churches; and in the time of Muhammad ﷺ the mosques.
His saying: ﴿وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَن يَنْصُرُهُ﴾, i.e. whoever upholds one of His laws is helped in upholding it — except that nothing is upheld in the law of a prophet except what that prophet brought, and one refrains from what he forbade.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ إنْ مَكَّنّاهم في الأرْضِ أقامُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: "الَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative as an explanation of "مَن". The meaning is: "Allah will surely help whoever helps Him"; then He made clear the description of His helpers and said: ﴿الَّذِينَ إنْ مَكَّنّاهم في الأرْضِ أقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ وأمَرُوا بِالمَعْرُوفِ ونَهَوْا عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾. So the description of Allah's party, those who affirm His oneness, is establishing prayer, giving zakāt, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. These two are obligatory just as prayer and zakāt are obligatory — I mean enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿فَكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ أهْلَكْناها وهي ظالِمَةٌ فَهي خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها﴾ — it is also read "أهْلَكْتُها". The meaning (connects with) ﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 44], i.e. then I seized them and carried My disapproval to its utmost, and I destroyed many towns; because the meaning of "فَكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ" is the meaning of "فَكَمْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ!" (how many a town!), and the meaning of "كَمْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ!" is a great number of towns.
"كَأيِّنْ" with doubled yāʾ is possible, and "كائِنٌ مِن قَرْيَةٍ" is possible. According to the Basrans it has the meaning of a large number: you say "وَكائِنٌ مِن رَجُلٍ جاءَنِي", meaning "a great number of men came to me". ﴿فَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها﴾: "العُرُوش" are the roofs. The meaning is that they have fallen to ruin and become empty, and have come to rest upon their roofs, as He said in another place: ﴿فَجَعَلْنا عالِيَها سافِلَها﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 74]. One says: "خَوَتِ الدّارُ" (the house became empty), and "the city is خَواء" — with the long vowel (mamdūd) — "so it is خاوِيَة"; and "خَوِيَتِ المَرْأةُ", and "خَوِيَ الإنْسانُ" — when one is empty of food — "خَوًى", with the short vowel (maqṣūr), "so he is خَوٍ".
His saying: ﴿وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ﴾: most of what has come in the exegesis concerning "مَشِيد" is "plastered with gypsum"; "الشِّيد" is gypsum, and lime is also shīd. It has also been said "مَشِيد" means fortified, lofty. "المُشَيَّد", when it is said to mean "plastered", is lofty in its standing even if it is not lofty in its height. The basic meaning of al-shīd is gypsum and quicklime, and everything built with both or with one of them is "مُشَيَّد".

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ تَعْمى القُلُوبُ الَّتِي في الصُّدُورِ﴾: the heart can only be in the breast, but this runs as tawkīd (emphasis), as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِأفْواهِهِمْ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 167], and as He said: ﴿وَلا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 38], and as some read: "لَهُ تِسْعٌ وتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةٌ". [Translator's note: as printed, the quotation shows no emphatic addition; the reading usually cited for this point is «نَعْجَةً أُنْثى», so a word has probably dropped out of the source.] So emphasis is current in speech and is a means of driving the meaning home.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ يَوْمًا عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ كَألْفِ سَنَةٍ مِمّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾: it has been said that one day of the days of their punishment is like a thousand years. This is indicated by the hadith which is narrated, that «the poor will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day», and in another hadith the explanation of this saying came as five hundred years; this indicates that a day of the days of the Resurrection is a thousand years.
What the verse indicates — and Allah knows best — is that they sought to hasten (the punishment), so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that nothing escapes Him, and that a day with Him and a thousand years are one in His power; and that in their seeking to hasten their appointed time there is no difference, as regards His power, between the occurrence of the punishment they seek to hasten and its being delayed — except that Allah, exalted be His praise, bestowed the favour of granting respite and forgave upon repentance. So the difference between delay and advancing it is Allah's favour, Mighty and Majestic is He, in granting respite.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He had seized peoples after granting them respite and delay, as a punishment from Him, so that they might increase in sin. He said after His saying ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالعَذابِ﴾ and after the completion of the verse: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ أمْلَيْتُ لَها وهي ظالِمَةٌ ثُمَّ أخَذْتُها وإلَيَّ المَصِيرُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 48]. The meaning is: "then I seized it with the punishment"; mention of the punishment was dispensed with because it had already been mentioned in His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالعَذابِ﴾.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ سَعَوْا في آياتِنا مُعاجِزِينَ﴾, i.e. thinking that they could frustrate Us, because they thought that they would not be raised, and that there is no Paradise and no Fire. It was said in the exegesis: "مُعاجِزِينَ" means obstinately opposing, and this is not outside the first view. It has also been read "مُعَجِّزِينَ", and its interpretation is that they used to try to make those who followed the Prophet ﷺ fall short, and to hold them back from him.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَسُولٍ ولا نَبِيٍّ إلا إذا تَمَنّى ألْقى الشَّيْطانُ في أُمْنِيَّتِهِ﴾: the meaning of "إذا تَمَنّى" is "when he recited"; "Satan cast into his recitation". That is a trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and He may try with whatever He wills. So Satan cast upon the tongue of the Prophet something of the description of the idols, and the people of discord and hypocrisy, and those in whose hearts is a disease, were tempted by it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِيَجْعَلَ ما يُلْقِي الشَّيْطانُ فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ والقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 53]. Then He made known that they are wrongdoers and that they are in perpetual discord — "الشِّقاق" is the utmost enmity — and said: ﴿وَإنَّ الظّالِمِينَ لَفي شِقاقٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 53].

zajjaj:55-55.t:
Then He made known that they will not repent, and said: ﴿وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا في مِرْيَةٍ مِنهُ﴾, i.e. in doubt about it, ﴿حَتّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ السّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾, i.e. suddenly, ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَهم عَذابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ﴾. The basic meaning of "العُقْم" is barrenness in childbearing. One says "this is a barren (عَقِيم) woman", as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 29]; likewise "a barren man" when he does not beget. The poet said:
؎عَقِيمَ النِّساءِ فَلا يَلِدْنَ شَبِيهَهُ إنَّ النِّساءَ بِمِثْلِهِ لَعَقِيمُ
(Women have become barren and do not bear his like; indeed women are barren of one like him.)
"The barren wind (الرِّيحُ العَقِيمُ)" is the one that brings no rain-giving cloud but brings only punishment; and "the barren day" is the one in which no good comes. So the Day of Resurrection is barren for the unbelievers, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَلى الكافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 10], and it is not so for the believers who have been admitted into Allah's mercy. Some of the lexicographers recited, concerning His saying "تَمَنّى" in the sense of "تَلا" (recited), the poet's saying:
؎تَمَنّى كِتابَ اللَّهِ أوَّلَ لَيْلِهِ ∗∗∗ وآخِرَهُ لاقى حِمامَ المَقادِرِ
(He recited the Book of Allah at the start of his night, and at its end met the death decreed.)
i.e. "he recited the Book of Allah slowly and deliberately", as Dāwūd recited the Psalms slowly and deliberately.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ ومَن عاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبَ بِهِ﴾: "ذَلِكَ" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is "the matter is that", i.e. the matter is what We have related to you. His saying: ﴿وَمَن عاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبَ بِهِ﴾: the first was not a punishment; punishment is only requital. But it was called punishment because the act which is punishment was a requital, so the first act, for which requital was made, was called punishment, since the two acts are alike in being of the genus of the hateful. As He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها﴾ [al-Shūrā: 40]: the first is an "evil deed", while the requital for it is a good deed among the good deeds of the one who requites it, except that it was called an evil deed because it fell as harm upon the one to whom it was done, since what was done to him was something that grieved him. Likewise His saying: ﴿مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 14] ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 15]: He made their requital for their mockery named with the word for their act, because it is the requital of their act.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ أنْـزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الأرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾ — it has also been read "مَخْضَرَةً". Allah, exalted be His praise, mentioned what indicates His oneness: making the night enter into the day and the day into the night; He mentioned His sending down water that makes things grow; He mentioned subjecting ships on the sea, and holding back the sky lest it fall upon the earth except by His leave. So He showed that He is the One who created creation and brought about what human beings cannot possibly bring the like of.
Then He mentioned the ignorance of the polytheists in their worship of idols, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَـزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطانًا﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 71], i.e. that for which He has sent down no proof, and of which they have no knowledge. Then He struck for them a parable of what they worship, and that it neither benefits nor harms. As for the reading, it is ﴿فَتُصْبِحُ الأرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾ and nothing else (i.e. with the nominative fa-tuṣbiḥu).
Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ أنْـزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الأرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾, and he said: this is an affirmative statement (wājib), and its meaning is drawing attention, as though He said: "Do you hear? Allah sent down water from the sky, and such-and-such happened." Someone else said the like of his saying: the construction of this speech is that of a declarative statement, as though He said: "Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green." And they recited:
؎ألَمْ تَسْألِ الرَّبْعَ القَواءَ فَيَنْطِقُ وهَلْ تُخْبِرَنْكَ اليَوْمَ بَيْداءُ سَمْلَقُ؟
(Did you not ask the deserted encampment — and it speaks? And will a barren, level desert tell you anything today?)
Al-Khalīl said: the meaning is "for it is something that speaks". As for whoever read "مَخْضَرَةً", it is in the sense of "having green growth (ذاتَ مَخْضَرَةٍ)", like "مَبْقَلَة", having herbs, and "مَشْبَعَة", having satiety. "مَخَضَرَّةً" with fatḥa on the mīm and doubled rāʾ is not permissible, because "مَفْعَلَّة" does not exist in the language and has no meaning.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكم ما في الأرْضِ والفُلْكَ تَجْرِي﴾: "الفُلْكَ" in the accusative is conjoined (nasaq) to "ما"; the meaning is "and He subjected to you the ships", and "تَجْرِي" is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He subjected the ships to you in the state of their sailing. It is also read "والفُلْكُ تَجْرِي في البَحْرِ بِأمْرِهِ", so that "الفُلْكُ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and "تَجْرِي" is the khabar (predicate); the meaning is still the meaning of subjection, because their sailing by His command is the subjection.
His saying: ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّماءَ أنْ تَقَعَ عَلى الأرْضِ إلا بِإذْنِهِ﴾ is in the sense of "out of aversion to its falling upon the earth". The position of "أنْ" is accusative through "يُمْسِكُ", and it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is "out of aversion to its falling".

zajjaj:67-67.t:
His saying: ﴿لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنا مَنسَكًا﴾, and "مَنسِكًا": the explanation of this has already been given.
His saying: ﴿فَلا يُنازِعُنَّكَ في الأمْرِ﴾, i.e. let them not dispute with you about it, and its meaning is: do not dispute with them; and the proof is that the meaning is "let them not dispute with you, and do not dispute with them". [Translator's note: the sentence appears incomplete in the source; it is continued in the next entry.]

zajjaj:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ جادَلُوكَ فَقُلِ اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: this was before (the command to) fight.
If someone asks: they did dispute with him, so why was it said "فَلا يُنازِعُنَّكَ في الأمْرِ" when they had disputed with him? The meaning is that it is a prohibition to him ﷺ against disputing with them, as one says: "Let so-and-so never contend with you in this." This is permissible with a verb that can only take place between two parties, because disputing and contending are only accomplished by two.
So when you say "لا يُجادِلَنَّكَ فُلانٌ" (let so-and-so not dispute with you), it stands in the place of "لا تُجادِلَنَّهُ" (do not dispute with him). This is not permissible in saying "لا يَضْرِبَنَّكَ فُلانٌ" (let so-and-so not hit you) when you mean "do not hit him"; but if you said "لا يُضارِبَنَّكَ فُلانٌ" (let so-and-so not exchange blows with you), it would be like your saying "لا تُضارِبَنَّ فُلانًا". It is also read "فَلا يَنْزِعُنَّكَ في الأمْرِ", meaning "let them not overcome you in disputing about it". One says: "نازَعَنِي فُلانٌ فَنَزَعْتُهُ" (so-and-so disputed with me and I overcame him in the dispute), and "عازَّنِي فَعَزَزْتُهُ" (he contended with me for mastery and I mastered him) — I overcome him and defeat him. The meaning is: "let them not overcome you in the matter".

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿يَكادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِالَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا﴾, i.e. they almost assault with violence the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, and those who recite the Qurʾān to them.
His saying: ﴿قُلْ أفَأُنَبِّئُكم بِشَرٍّ مِن ذَلِكُمُ النّارُ وعَدَها اللَّهُ﴾: the reading is with the nominative, and it is grammatically sounder than the genitive and the accusative, though the genitive and accusative are permissible. Whoever reads the nominative takes it in the sense of "it is the Fire" (هُوَ النّارُ / هِيَ النّارُ), as though they said: "What is this which is worse?", and it was said: "The Fire." Whoever says "النّارِ" in the genitive takes it as a badal (substitute) for "شَرٍّ". Whoever says "النّارَ" in the accusative takes it in the sense of "I mean the Fire", or in the sense of "أُنَبِّئُكم بِشَرٍّ مِن ذَلِكُمْ", as though He said: "I shall make known to you something worse than that: the Fire."

zajjaj:73-74.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ﴾: because they worshipped besides Allah what neither hears nor sees, and that for which He sent down no proof, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them the answer concerning what they set up as a likeness to Allah and made a peer to Him, and said: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُبابًا ولَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا لَهُ﴾ — meaning the idols and everyone who is invoked as a god besides Allah; there is no god but Allah alone.
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ الذُّبابُ شَيْئًا لا يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ مِنهُ﴾: Allah, exalted be His praise, made known that He is the Creator, and pointed to His oneness by everything He has created; then He made known that those worshipped besides Him are not able to create one small, weak creature of His creation, nor to recover something trivial and insignificant from it.
Then He said: ﴿ما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾, i.e. they have not magnified Him as His greatness truly deserves. Then, after mentioning the weakness of the strength of those worshipped, He made known His own strength and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾.
His saying: ﴿ضَعُفَ الطّالِبُ والمَطْلُوبُ﴾: "ضَعُفَ" and "ضُعِفَ الطّالِبُ والمَطْلُوبُ" are both possible, i.e. "they are too weak to create a fly and to recover anything from the fly — with the weakness of the fly."

zajjaj:75-75.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ رُسُلا ومِنَ النّاسِ﴾: Allah chose from among the angels Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death, and He chose from among people the prophets and the messengers — may Allah bless them and grant them peace, all of them.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا واسْجُدُوا واعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. intend by your bowing and your prostration Allah alone. ﴿وافْعَلُوا الخَيْرَ﴾: "الخَيْر" (good) is everything Allah has commanded.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾: this is not doubt; rather its meaning is "so that you may hope to be on the path of success", as He said to Mūsā and Hārūn: ﴿اذْهَبا إلى فِرْعَوْنَ إنَّهُ طَغى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 43] ﴿فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أوْ يَخْشى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 44], i.e. go in your hope, just as a prophet hopes regarding those to whom he is sent — while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, encompasses the knowledge of what Pharaoh's affair will come to; except that the proof is only established after clear explanation.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجاهِدُوا في اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ﴾: it has been said that it is on a par with His saying: ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 102], and that it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ما اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 16].
His saying: ﴿هُوَ اجْتَباكُمْ﴾ means: He has chosen you.
His saying: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكم في الدِّينِ مِن حَرَجٍ﴾, i.e. any constriction. Allah has prescribed, for one who is unable to do something that is burdensome at a given time, what is lighter than it. So breaking the fast while travelling was granted to the one fasting; and the shortening of prayer; and for the one praying, if he cannot stand, that he pray sitting, and if he cannot sit, that he pray by gestures. He permitted a man to marry four, and permitted him all that his right hand possesses. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made things spacious for His creation.
His saying: ﴿مِلَّةَ أبِيكم إبْراهِيمَ﴾ means: follow the religion of your father Ibrāhīm. It is also possible that it is accusative through His saying: "worship your Lord and do good, (like) the doing of your father Ibrāhīm".
His saying: ﴿هُوَ سَمّاكُمُ المُسْلِمِينَ مِن قَبْلُ وفي هَذا﴾: "هُوَ" refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The meaning is: "Allah named you Muslims before He sent down the Qurʾān, and in this Qurʾān He named you Muslims." It is also possible that it was Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, who named you Muslims before; "وَفِي هَذا", i.e. Ibrāhīm judged that everyone who believes in Muhammad, affirming the oneness of Allah — Ibrāhīm has named him a "Muslim".
His saying: ﴿وَتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلى النّاسِ﴾: it is narrated «that Allah, Glorified is He, gave this community three things which none but the prophets were given: it was made a witness over all the other communities, whereas the witnessing (had been) for each prophet over his community; and it used to be said to a prophet, peace be upon him: (Go, and there is no constraint upon you), while Allah said to this community: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكم في الدِّينِ مِن حَرَجٍ﴾; and He said to every prophet: (Ask and you will be given it), while He said to this community: ﴿وَقالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 60]».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥajj (The Pilgrimage)
Meccan
﷽
His words: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾ — ”يا أيُّها“ is a vague, singular vocative; ”ها“ is for drawing attention, and [”أيُّ“] is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma. ”اَلنّاسُ“ is nominative, following ”يا أيُّها“. The grammarians permit only the nominative of ”اَلنّاسُ“ here; al-Māzinī permitted the accusative in ”يا أيُّها الرَّجُلَ أقْبِلْ“ ("O you man, come forward"), just as you say ”يا زَيْدَ الظَّرِيفَ، والظَّرِيفُ“ ("O Zayd the elegant", accusative and nominative). This is an error on al-Māzinī's part, because with ”زَيْدًا“ one may stop and be content with it without ”اَلظَّرِيفُ“, whereas ”يا أيُّها“ is not [complete] speech: what is intended is ”اَلنّاسُ“, so it is as though it were ”يا ناسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ“ ("O people, fear your Lord").
It has come in the exegesis that everything in the Book of Allah beginning ”يا أيُّها النّاسُ“ is Meccan, and whatever has ”يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا“ is Medinan.
And His words: ﴿إنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ — it was said that this earthquake is in this world, and that after it comes the rising of the sun from its place of setting. It was also said that it is the earthquake that accompanies the Hour.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
﴿يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمّا أرْضَعَتْ﴾ — ”تُذْهِلُ كُلَّ مُرْضِعَةٍ“ is also permissible. The meaning of ”تُذْهِلُ“ is: it bewilders, and leaves every nursing woman distracted from what she was nursing. ”مُرْضِعَةٍ“ follows the pattern ”اَلْمُفْعِلُ“ [with the feminine ending] according to [the act of] her nursing. One says ”اِمْرَأةٌ مُرْضِعٌ“, i.e. a woman possessed of suckling, whether she nursed her own child or nursed another; and the intention is that of ”مُلْبِنٌ“, i.e. one having milk.
And His words: ﴿وَتَرى النّاسَ سُكارى﴾ — it has also been read ”وَتَرى النّاسُ سَكْرى“. The agent is implied in ”تَرى“; the meaning is: ”تَرى أنْتَ أيُّها الإنْسانُ النّاسَ“ ("you, O man, see the people"). Whoever reads ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سَكْرى“, it is equivalent to ”وَتَرى أنْتَ النّاسَ سَكْرى“ ("and you see the people drunk"). There is another form, which has been read [Translator's note: «ما قُرِئَ بِهِ» may also mean "which has not been read"], namely ”وَيُرى النّاسُ سَكْرى“ ("and the people are seen drunk"), in which ”اَلنّاسُ“ is the noun of ”يُرى“ [its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; and another form that has not been read: ”وَيَرى النّاسَ سَكْرى“, the meaning being ”وَيَرى الإنْسانُ النّاسَ سَكْرى“ ("and man sees the people drunk").
It is read ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سَكْرى وما هم بِسَكْرى“ and ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سُكارى وما هم بِسُكارى“; and ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سَكارى وما هم بِسَكارى“ is permissible. The frequent reading is ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سَكْرى وما هم بِسُكْرى“ [Translator's note: so printed], and also ”وَتَرى النّاسَ سُكارى وما هم بِسُكارى“. The interpretation is that you see them as if drunk from the punishment and fear, but they are not drunk from drink; and what indicates this is: ﴿وَلَكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ﴾.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And His words: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يُجادِلُ في اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ ويَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ﴾, i.e. he follows what the devil makes attractive to him. ”مَرِيدٌ“ and ”مارِدٌ“ mean that he has become hardened (marada) in evil.
The interpretation of ”اَلْمَرْوَدُ“ [Translator's note: so printed; «اَلْمُرُودُ», "hardening in rebellion", is probably meant] is reaching the limit by which one departs from the general condition of one's kind. It may be used of other than the devil: you say ”قَدْ تَمَرَّدَ هَذا السَّيِّئُ“ ("this evil one has become rebellious"), i.e. ”قَدْ جاوَزَ حَدَّ مِثْلِهِ“ ("he has exceeded the limit of his like"). Its basic sense in the language is smoothness of a thing: from it is your saying of a person ”أمْرَدُ“ ("beardless") when there is no hair on his face, and a rock is called ”مَرْداءُ“ when it is smooth.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أنَّهُ مَن تَوَلاهُ﴾ — ”أنَّهُ“ is in the position of the nominative [as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of ”كُتِبَ“]. ﴿فَأنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ﴾ is conjoined to it, and its position is also nominative. The best view of the fāʾ is that it is in the sense of the response to the condition (jazāʾ). The kasra of ”إنَّ“ with the fāʾ is also permissible, and then it is the response to the condition and nothing else. The interpretation is: ”كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ - أيْ: عَلى الشَّيْطانِ - إضْلالُ مُتَوَلِّيهِ، وهِدايَتُهم إلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ“ ("it has been decreed for him — i.e. for the devil — that he misleads whoever takes him as patron and guides them to the punishment of the Blaze"). The real nature of the second ”أنَّ“ is that it is a repetition of the first, by way of tawkīd (emphasis), because the meaning is: ”كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أنَّهُ مَن تَوَلّاهُ أضَلَّهُ“ ("it is decreed for him that whoever takes him as patron, he misleads him").

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His words: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ في رَيْبٍ مِنَ البَعْثِ﴾ — it is also read ”مِنَ البَعَثِ“, with a fatḥa on the ʿayn. ”اَلرَّيْبُ“ is doubt. As for ”اَلْبَعَثُ“ with a fatḥa on the ʿayn: all the Kufans mention that any word whose second letter is one of the guttural letters, quiescent, with a fatḥa on the first letter, may have the quiescent letter given a fatḥa, as in ”نَعْلٌ“ / ”نَعَلٌ“ (sandal), ”شَعْرٌ“ / ”شَعَرٌ“ (hair), ”نَهْرٌ“ / ”نَهَرٌ“ (river), and ”نَخْلٌ“ / ”نَخَلٌ“ (palms). The Basrans, however, hold that whatever of this has come with both dialectal forms is spoken as it has come, and whatever has not been heard may not be given a vowel, as in ”وَعْدٌ“: for you do not say ”لَكَ عَلَيَّ وعَدٌ“ meaning ”عَلَيَّ وِعْدَةٌ“ ("I owe you a promise"), nor ”فِي هَذا الأمْرِ وهَنٌ“ in the sense of ”وَهْنٌ“ ("there is weakness in this matter"). This, in its category, is like ”رَكٌّ“ / ”رَكَكٌ“, ”قِدْرٌ“ / ”قَدَرٌ“, and ”قَصُّ الشّاةِ“ / ”قَصَصُها“ (the sheep's breastbone); so there is no difference in this between the guttural letters and others.
It was said to those who denied the resurrection — the polytheists: if you are in doubt that Allah raises the dead, then reflect upon the matter of your creation and your beginning, for you will find no difference in power between originating creation and bringing it back and giving life to the dead. Then He explained to them the beginning of their creation, informing them that they were created from dust — that is the creation of Ādam, peace be upon him — then the creation of his offspring from a drop of semen (nuṭfa), then from a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then from a lump of flesh (muḍgha); and He informed them of the stages of their creation. It is related that a human being is in the womb a nuṭfa for forty days, then a muḍgha for forty days, then Allah sends an angel who breathes the spirit into him. [Translator's note: the ʿalaqa stage of forty days is absent from the text at this point.] The meaning of ﴿مُخَلَّقَةٍ وغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾ is a description of the creation: or [i.e.] among them are those whose muḍgha is completed, so that there are created for him the limbs that complete the faculties of a human being, and among them are those whose creation Allah does not complete.
And His words: ﴿لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾, i.e. We have mentioned the stages of the creation of man [to make clear to you]. Another view is: ”خَلَقْناكم هَذا الخَلْقَ لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ“ ("We created you with this creation to make clear to you"). ﴿وَنُقِرُّ في الأرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ﴾ — only the nominative is permissible in it; it cannot mean ”فَعَلْنا ذَلِكَ لِنُقِرَّ في الأرْحامِ“ ("We did that so that We might settle in the wombs"), for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, did not create mankind for what is settled in the wombs; He created them only to guide them to their right course and their welfare.
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكم طِفْلا﴾ — in the sense of ”أطْفالًا“ ("infants"); the mention of the plural indicates that, and it is as though ”طِفْلًا“ indicates the sense of ”وَيُخْرَجُ كُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنكم طِفْلًا“ ("each one of you is brought out as an infant").
﴿ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أشُدَّكُمْ﴾ — we have already explained al-ashudd; its interpretation is perfection in strength and discernment, and it is between thirty and forty.
And His words: ﴿وَمِنكم مَن يُرَدُّ إلى أرْذَلِ العُمُرِ﴾ — ”أرْذَلُ العُمُرِ“ is the age at which a person becomes senile from old age, until he does not understand; He made that clear by His saying: ﴿لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِن بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ﴾. Then He pointed them to His giving life to the dead through His giving life to the earth, saying: ﴿وَتَرى الأرْضَ هامِدَةً﴾, meaning dry, dusty. ﴿فَإذا أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْها الماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ ورَبَتْ﴾ — it is also read ”وَرَبَأتْ“. Its stirring is its moving when the water falls on it, and its sprouting. Whoever reads ”وَرَبَتْ“, it is from ”رَبا، يَرْبُو“ when something increases in any direction; whoever reads ”وَرَبَأتْ“ with the hamza, its meaning is "it rose". ﴿وَأنْبَتَتْ مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ﴾, i.e. of every beautiful kind of plant.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ هو الحَقُّ وأنَّهُ يُحْيِي المَوْتى وأنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ — the meaning is: ”اَلْأمْرُ ذَلِكَ“ ("the matter is that"), i.e. ”اَلْأمْرُ ما وُصِفَ لَكُمْ، وبُيِّنَ لَكُمْ، بِأنَّ اللَّهَ هو الحَقُّ وأنَّهُ يُحْيِي المَوْتى، وأنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ“ ("the matter is what has been described and made clear to you, because Allah is the Truth, He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things"). So the best view is that the position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative; it may also be accusative, in the sense of ”فَعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُ هو الحَقُّ، وأنَّهُ يُحْيِي المَوْتى“ ("Allah did that because He is the Truth and He gives life to the dead").

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His words: ﴿ثانِيَ عِطْفِهِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — also ”وَلِيَضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ“. ”ثانِيَ“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); its sense is that of tanwīn [i.e. the annexation is not a real one], and its meaning is ”ثانِيًا عِطْفَهُ“ ("turning his side"). It has come in the exegesis that its meaning is ”لاوِيًا عُنُقَهُ“ ("twisting his neck"), and this is used to describe [arrogance]; so the meaning is: ”وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يُجادِلُ في اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ مُتَكَبِّرًا“ ("among people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge, being arrogant").

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ وأنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ — it is said [to him]: ”هَذا العَذابُ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ“ ("this punishment is for what your hands have sent ahead"). The position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ”بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ“. The position of ”أنَّ“ is genitive; the meaning is: ”ذَلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ وبِأنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ“ ("that is for what your hands have sent ahead, and because Allah is not unjust to the servants"). If it were read ”إنَّ“ with the kasra, it would be permissible. It is also possible that the position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: ”اَلْأمْرُ ذَلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ“ ("the matter is that, for what your hands have sent ahead"), and that the position of ”أنَّ“ is nominative, in the sense of ”أنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ“ [i.e. "and [the matter is] that Allah is not unjust to the servants"].

zajjaj:11-11.t: His words: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلى حَرْفٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis: ”عَلى شَكٍّ“ ("in doubt"). Its real sense is that he worships Allah on the edge of the path in religion, not entering it as one firmly settled. ﴿فَإنْ أصابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأنَّ بِهِ﴾, i.e. if fertility comes to him and his wealth and livestock increase, he is content with what has come to him and pleased with his religion. ﴿وَإنْ أصابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾: a test through drought and little wealth, ﴿انْقَلَبَ عَلى وجْهِهِ﴾: he turns back from his religion to disbelief and the worship of idols.

zajjaj:12-12.t: And His words: ﴿يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَضُرُّهُ وما لا يَنْفَعُهُ﴾ — meaning: ”يَدْعُو الوَثَنَ الَّذِي لا يَسْمَعُ، ولا يُبْصِرُ، ولا يَنْفَعُ، ولا يَضُرُّ“ ("he calls upon the idol, which neither hears nor sees, neither benefits nor harms").

zajjaj:13-13.t:
And His words: ﴿يَدْعُو لَمَن ضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ﴾ — He said ”وَلا يَضُرُّهُ“ ("and does not harm him") and [then] said ”ضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ“ ("his harm is nearer than his benefit"); its meaning is: ”اَلضَّرَرُ بِعِبادَتِهِ أقْرَبُ مِنَ النَّفْعِ“ ("the harm from worshipping it is nearer than the benefit").
If someone asks: How can it be said ”أقَرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهُ“ ("nearer than its benefit") when there is no benefit whatsoever from it? [The answer is that] the Arabs say of what will not happen: ”هَذا بَعِيدٌ“ ("this is far-off"); the evidence for that is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ﴾ [Qāf: 3].
People have disagreed over the interpretation of this lām, and over ”يَدْعُو“ — to what it is attached. We shall explain all that they said, and what they overlooked that is clear from all they said, if Allah wills.
The Basrans and the Kufans said: the lām is in the sense of deferment; the meaning is: ”يَدْعُو مَن لَضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ“ ("he calls upon one whose harm is indeed nearer than his benefit"). But they did not give a full explanation, nor did they say how it is permissible for the lām to be out of its place. The explanation of that is that the lām is for the oath and emphasis, so its due place is at the beginning of the speech; therefore it was brought forward so as to be put in its due place, even though its original place is in ”لَضَرُّهُ“ — just as the lām of ”إنَّ“ belongs by right at the beginning [of the nominal sentence].
Since it may not directly follow ”إنَّ“, it was put in the khabar (predicate), as in your saying ”إنَّ زَيْدًا لَقائِمٌ“ ("Zayd is indeed standing"); ”إنَّ لَزَيْدًا قائِمٌ“ is not permissible. When it is possible for it to be in the noun, that is the best usage: you say ”إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً“ ("in that there is indeed a sign"). That is one view.
They also said: ”يَدْعُو“ has an implied [object] hāʾ with it, and ”ذَلِكَ“ [in the preceding verse] is in the position of the nominative, with ”يَدْعُو“ in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: ”ذَلِكَ هو الضَّلالُ البَعِيدُ يَدْعُوهُ“ ("that is the far straying, calling upon it"), meaning ”فِي حالِ دُعائِهِ إيّاهُ“ ("in the state of his calling upon it"). Then ”لَمَن ضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ“ is resumptive, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar is: ﴿لَبِئْسَ المَوْلى ولَبِئْسَ العَشِيرُ﴾.
There is another, third, possibility: ”يَدْعُو“ is in the sense of ”يَقُولُ“ ("he says"), ”مَن“ is in the position of the nominative and its khabar is omitted, the meaning being: ”يَقُولُ: لَمَن ضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ، هو مَوْلايَ“ ("he says: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit — he is my patron"). Similar to it — ”يَدْعُو“ in the sense of ”يَقُولُ“ — is the saying of ʿAntara:
؎يَدْعُونَ عَنْتَرُ والرِّماحُ كَأنَّها أشْطانُ بِئْرٍ في لَبانِ الأدْهَمِ
(They cry "ʿAntar!" while the spears, like the ropes of a well, are in the chest of the black steed.)
It is also possible that ”يَدْعُو“ is in the sense of ”يُسَمِّي“ ("he names"), as Ibn Aḥmar said:
؎أهْوى لَها مِشْقَصًا حَشْرًا فَشَبْرَقَها ∗∗∗ وكُنْتُ أدْعُو قَذاها الإثْمِدَ القَرِدا
(He aimed at it a slender broad-headed arrow and tore it apart — and I used to call the mote in its eye clumped antimony.)
The sense of this view is the same as the one before it.
There is a fourth possibility in it, which is the one people have overlooked: that ”ذَلِكَ“ is in the position of the accusative because ”يَدْعُو“ falls upon it [as its mafʿūl bihi (direct object)], with ”ذَلِكَ“ having the interpretation of ”اَلَّذِي“ ("that which"), so the meaning is: ”اَلَّذِي هو الضَّلالُ البَعِيدُ يَدْعُو“ ("he calls upon that which is the far straying"), and ”لَمَن ضَرُّهُ أقْرَبُ مِن نَفْعِهِ“ is resumptive. This is like His saying: ﴿وَما تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 17], in the sense of ”وَما الَّتِي بِيَمِينِكَ يا مُوسى ؟“ ("and what is that which is in your right hand, O Mūsā?"); and similar to it is the saying of the poet:
؎عَدَسْ ما لِعَبّادٍ عَلَيْكَ إمارَةٌ ∗∗∗ نَجَوْتِ وهَذا تَحْمِلِينَ طَلِيقُ
(Gee up! ʿAbbād has no authority over you; you have escaped, and this one whom you carry is free.)
